extracted.intended_audience: NSA leadership and Intelligence Community officials responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on applying Draft OMB Circular A-76 (performance of commercial activities) to intelligence agencies, particularly assessing when activities should remain in-house due to security concerns and how to escalate unresolved compliance conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No formal agency exemptions from Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: "No agency has been formally exempted from compliance with Circular A-76, nor is any likely to be."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempts to secure a formal exemption from OMB are unlikely to succeed; agencies should plan to comply with the Circular rather than expect an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security risk can justify in‑house performance
rubrics_metrics.description: "While an activity may not be justified for in-house operation solely because it involves or supports a classified program, the fact that an inordinate security risk would result from having a contractor perform the activity would most probably be considered by OMB to be adequate justification."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency should evaluate whether contractor performance would create an "inordinate security risk." If so, that security risk is likely a valid basis for retaining the activity in-house under A-76. Merely supporting a classified program is not alone sufficient justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation if compliance threatens security interests
rubrics_metrics.description: "If [an agency] runs into significant difficulty in complying with A-76, and cannot reach a reasonable agreement with OMB which would protect its security interests, [senior leadership] will recommend that the DCI intervene directly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency-level negotiations with OMB cannot secure protections for sensitive sources/methods, agencies should document the difficulty and pursue escalation to senior Intelligence Community leadership (DCI) for direct intervention.
